title: Microsoft 365 account takeover cleanup
product: Microsoft Entra ID and Exchange Online
use_case: When a Microsoft 365 account is taken over, reset the user's password to a random one, revoke their sign-in sessions, make them change their password at the next sign-in, turn off inbox rules that forward, redirect or delete mail, confirm them as compromised in Entra ID where the tenant has Entra ID P2, and record the inbox rules before and after on the case.
trigger: Platform Events, source Identity Findings, event Created, or source Alert2 (detections), event create, each with the Only When filter in SETUP.md. Or User Initiated, a Response Action on Case, to run it by hand from a case.
connections: Taegis.MicrosoftGraphAPI 2.12.2, the Microsoft Graph API connector Sophos manages, to look users up, reset and expire passwords, revoke sessions, turn off inbox rules and confirm compromise
Taegis.Case 1.0.5 and Taegis.Alert 1.3.6, the case and detection connectors Sophos manages, to read the case's detections and add the comment
requires: Microsoft 365 with Exchange Online mailboxes, a Microsoft Graph API connection with the permissions in SETUP.md, Entra ID P2 in the tenant for Confirm compromised (skipped without it), Sophos ITDR for the identity finding trigger, and Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook, and Sophos MDR may already be acting on the same user. A run from a case acts only on self-managed cases unless you turn on Include Sophos-managed cases. The identity finding and detection triggers don't check who works the detection, so agree them with the Sophos MDR team first.
rollback: Turn the inbox rules back on (the case comment names them), enable the account if Disable account was on, and dismiss the user's risk in Entra ID. Revoked sessions stay revoked and the old password can't be restored, so the user signs in with a new one from your helpdesk or self-service password reset.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook cleans up a taken-over Microsoft 365 account: it resets the user's password to a random one, revokes their sessions, makes them change it at the next sign-in, turns off inbox rules that forward, redirect or delete mail, confirms them as compromised where the tenant has Entra ID P2, and comments the rules before and after. It runs on a Sophos ITDR leaked credential finding, a Microsoft detection or by hand from a case, through the Microsoft Graph API connector. Dry run is on.
notes:
Setup:
- Confirm compromised needs Entra ID P2 in the tenant, not on the user, so a P1-only user is confirmed where the tenant has P2. Without P2 it skips the step and says why.
- Leave the connection's Password to use in response actions setting at its default, a new random password for each reset: a fixed value gives every reset user the same password.
- There is no Active Directory step: Fusion wants a connection for every connector a template lists. The comment flags synced users.
- Ask for approval first holds every change for an approval through the chat bridge and Approval before acting. A finding run has no case, so it then does nothing.

How it works:
- It resets the password before revoking sessions, and keeps the reset's request out of the execution log, so the new password isn't recorded.
- A finding run acts on the finding's user, a detection run on its userName entities with an @ (or targetUserName), and a run from a case on the users in all of the case's detections.
- It turns off an inbox rule only when the rule is on and forwards, redirects or deletes mail. Rules that only move or mark mail are left on.

Testing:
- The dsl passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings in us01 and eu02 (2026-11-15, 1.2.0 on 2026-11-16).
- In us01 a renamed copy ran 15 times on a test Microsoft 365 user through the Marketplace connection, with made-up detections and finding and a test case: it revoked sessions, required a password change, disabled the account and turned off forward, redirect and delete rules. Entra ID, the mailbox and the audit log were read back. Dry run, limits, exclusions and unknown users held.
- After the reset the old password was refused and the execution log held no password. With Entra ID P2 in the tenant it confirmed a P2 and a P1-only user; on P1 alone 1.1.0 skipped the step and ended SUCCESS.
- On 2026-11-16, with a connection that may not reset passwords, 1.1.1's reset failed and the password change call still ran; the run ended FAIL naming both.
- 1.2.0 with Ask for approval first changed nothing until an approval through the chat bridge, then Approval before acting ran each step, read back in Entra ID, the mailbox and the audit log.

Known gaps:
- No real ITDR finding or Microsoft detection was used, and the case menu run wasn't tested: the API refuses User Initiated runs.
- MFA methods, OAuth app consents and Exchange Online forwarding aren't covered. A synced user wasn't tested.
